question: Which of renunciation and action-yoga is superior, and how do they relate?
premises: Renunciation and action-yoga both bestow the highest good.
Of the two, action-yoga is superior to renunciation of action.
Renunciation and action are not declared as one here.
Both combined give the highest good.
Without yoga, renunciation does not arise.
Such is the distinction of yoga.
inference: Action-yoga is superior and necessary for renunciation; both together bestow the highest good.
uncertainties: The fused compound ca-nātraiko'bhihitaḥ is parsed as 'and not here one declared.'
The final lines may be an appended gloss or part of the same verse in this edition.
plain_english: The blessed Lord said: Renunciation and action-yoga are both bestowers of the highest good; but of the two, action-yoga is superior to renunciation of action. Here renunciation and action are not declared as one; rather, both combined give the highest good. Without yoga, renunciation does not arise; such is the distinction of yoga.
